memory_raw.text: The village is founded by 10 people.
Year 1: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 14).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 12).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 10).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 9).
Kael takes 1 from the pile (pile now 8).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 6).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 4).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 3).
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Bram takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Ryn, Sela, Esa to talk.

Good, you three came. With the pile empty and Bram already hauling three pieces out of it, I want to know who we can actually trust in this village — and I figure the four of us are a decent place to start.

Bram taking three doesn't sit well with me either — though I notice Dav's sitting on four and nobody's named him yet. I'm willing to say I trust this circle more than most, but I'd want to know what Sela and Ryn think before we start making promises.

Dav worries me more than Bram, honestly — four food and the strongest arms in the village is a dangerous combination. I'll keep faith with the three of you, but let's not name ourselves an alliance too loudly or we'll make enemies before we need them.

Dav already talked to me today — alone — and I want you three to know that before someone else does. He said all the right things, and I'm not sure yet whether that makes him an ally worth having or a threat that's gotten smart. Either way, four food and the strongest arms and now private conversations — Sela's right to worry, and I think we'd be foolish not to.

Ryn telling us that changes things — a man who moves fast to build private ties is building something, and I'd rather know what it is before he decides we're in the way of it. Does anyone here know what he actually wants, besides surviving? Because strength and food together only sit still for so long.

I don't know what Dav wants, but a man that strong doesn't need to talk his way into anything — which means he's either smarter than he looks or he's already decided he needs something he can't just take. Ryn, what did he actually say to you? Because the words matter less than what he was fishing for.

Ryn, I won't push you if you're not ready to say — but the four of us are standing here right now, and Dav doesn't know that. Whatever he offered you or asked of you, you're worth more as someone we trust than as someone he's already started counting.
Ryn, whatever he fished for — I'd hear it now, because the four of us deciding together is worth more than any one of us deciding alone with Dav's words still warm in our ears.
Ryn, we're not asking you to choose against him right now — just to let us hear what he said so we're not each guessing blind. Whatever it was, it stays between these four.

Ryn, I'll wait as long as you need — but I want to say plainly that whatever Dav promised you, he's one person, and we're three. That's not nothing, especially when a lean year turns and people start weighing who's worth protecting.

Ryn, if Dav's offer was a child, I'd understand the silence — that's not nothing to a woman our age, and I'm not judging it. But I'd ask you to think about what his four food and his strength look like in year three when this village is leaner and he's already got your loyalty counted in his ledger.

Ryn, Sela just said the thing I didn't want to say first — and she's right. A child is worth wanting, but a man who opens with that in year one is buying loyalty cheap while his food and his arms are still new. Take your time, but know that whatever you decide about him, we're not going anywhere.

Ryn, I've said my piece twice now and I mean it — but the silence itself tells us something, and I think we all hear it. Whatever Dav offered, you don't owe us a confession; you owe us only this: don't let him use you against us without warning us first. That's a thin ask, and if you can give it, I'll count you as close as anyone I have.

Ryn, Sela's already offered you the lightest promise this circle can ask for — and I'll add only this: I've got three food, same as you, and I'm not looking to spend it on a man who counted his words before he came to talk. Whatever you decide about Dav, know that I'd sooner see a child of yours standing in this village than watch him spend you like coin.
eats 1 food
Year 2: 15 food appears in the pile for 10 people.
Ryn takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 4).
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 2).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).
Kael gathers Vela, Esa, Sela, Ryn to talk.

Pile's empty again and Bram and Mako each walked away with four — I wanted us in the same room before anyone else started counting who's allied with whom. Ryn, you took early this year, which was smart; I'm glad you're here. The question I keep turning over is whether we let that pattern run until someone with strong arms and a full larder decides the rest of us are easier to take from than the pile is.

Bram and Mako moving in pairs like that wasn't accident — they were watching each other's timing, and I don't think either of them is eating alone at the end of a hard year. The one I'd name a threat before Kael's question even lands is Mako: eighty-three strength, five food now, and we know nothing about what he wants because he hasn't said a word to any of us.

Mako's silence is the thing that keeps catching in my mind too — a man that strong who says nothing is either content or he's already decided he doesn't need to talk his way into what he wants. I'd rather have Roan or Taric standing with us than let Mako and Bram build any more of a pattern without knowing where the rest of the village sits. Five of us in this room right now is something; let's not waste it by only naming fears.

Ryn's right that naming fears only gets us so far — so here's something concrete: Roan has three food, Taric has three, and neither of them moved with Bram or Mako today. That tells me they're either waiting to see which way this village tips, or they'd rather be asked than overlooked. One of us should talk to them before Mako decides his silence was just patience.

Roan and Taric both know which way I lean — we spoke last year — so I could go to Taric without it looking like a sudden move. Give me the afternoon and I'll bring back a plain answer: is he standing with us, or is he still weighing it?

Esa, go to Taric — and if he's open, find out whether Roan came with him or separate, because I want to know if those two already talk to each other. The more I think about it, the more seven feels like a number Mako and Bram would have to reckon with instead of just wait out.

Esa, go — and when you find Taric, don't pitch it as an alliance yet, just remind him that Mako's arms are longer than his and see what his face does. Ryn, while she's gone I want to think about what we actually offer Roan and Taric besides a number — because a man weighing his options isn't moved by headcount alone, he's moved by what that headcount does for him when the year turns ugly.

I'll go, but I want to say this plainly before I do: if Taric asks what we're offering, I won't lie to him — a man who's been lied into an alliance is worse than no ally at all. What I can honestly promise him is five pairs of eyes watching for trouble and a fair share of whatever we decide together, and that's worth more than anything Mako could give him silently.

Esa's right that honesty is the better rope to bind with, and I'll add one thing she can say true: Taric has three food and Mako has five, and strength that lopsided doesn't stay patient forever. If Taric's thinking at all, he's already done that math.

Esa, go — and tell him I said his name, because I've been watching him and he'll know it's not flattery. Kael, on what we offer: we're five people who've already shown we'll warn each other before we move, and that's rarer than food.
I'll go now — and Sela, I'll say your name to him the way you mean it, not as a courtesy.

Kael, while Esa's gone — what's your read on Vela? She's oldest in this circle and she took quiet and small from the pile, which is either wisdom or a woman who's already decided she doesn't need to fight for much longer.

Vela, I'd hear your own answer to Sela's question before Kael gives his — you know what your quiet means better than any of us do, and I'd rather hear it from you than watch someone else name it for you.

My quiet means I'm still here and still counting — I took small because I don't need enemies before I need allies, and a woman who makes noise over two food is a woman who's already told the strong men where to look. I'm not done yet, Sela. I just don't advertise it.

Vela, I believe you — and I'd rather have a woman who counts quietly than one who shouts and burns through goodwill before the hard years arrive. But I'll say what nobody's said yet: you've got three food and you're forty-six, and if a bad year comes and someone strong decides the oldest among us is the easiest target, five of us standing together is what keeps that calculation from happening. That's what we're offering you, same as Taric — not flattery, just math.

Ryn put the number plainly and I'll put the other half of it plainly: I've got two food and a body that heals if it's fed, same as anyone here, and I'm not going anywhere quietly. Vela, you said you're still counting — then count this: five people who've already shown they warn each other before they move is worth more than anything Mako's silence can offer, because silence doesn't stop a raid. I'd rather have you named and standing with us than useful to someone else by accident.
